searchText: What is the plan for submitting 1559 transactions over JSON-RPC? Were we going to introduce a new method for `sendTransaction`, or just overload the existing one? <@135612611923279872> makes a good point at https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/rfc-signer-feature-detection-over-json-rpc/5773/3 that overloading an existing method makes it very difficult for wallets to identify whether or not the node they are speaking to supports 1559 transactions or not. e.g., right now they would have to hard code Ropsten to have support while Kovan does not have support and then have that change at some point in the future. If we introduce a new `eth_sendTransactionWithMaxFee` then they can (in theory) just detect whether that method is supported or not. Hi <@!552133098075193354> <@!301186049323958275> , do you anticipate any client implementation delays or any other delays for 1559? I was just curious about it based on the delays we have seen in the past for various HFs London *has* to happen in July. Whether 1559 gets included or not is still a bit up in the air but I think it probably will make it. got it. If it does not make it in London, will there be a special HF to implement it or would it be targeted directly for Shanghai? Well, if 1559 does not make it, then it would just be the difficulty bomb push out, right? I probably wouldn’t want to distinguish the fee by API method, as this puts submission logic in the hands of an app, which doesn’t need to be concerned with it. The same way we trust wallets to help users set gas, I think it’s ok for Ðapps to remain gas payment oblivious, but signers still need to know from a given node whether it accepts a feature, especially a tx-critical one, at the very least. Sorry, I was referring to the API you use for talking to the Ethereum client. Not the API you expose to your users. We use sendRawTransaction, sending a fully signed binary tx. I guess tx envelope and 1559 could use a new sendRawTransactionEnvelope method? But if nodes will accept a tx, then it’s a tx, not sure that part makes a big difference to signers, as long as they know which forms are supported. Oh, good point. Forgot that you use raw transaction endpoint. 🤔 It does feel like we need stronger versioning on this front somehow. Or capability detection at least. I now better understand why you want to ask the client "what *features* do you support?"
